title: Platform Developer I
description: Apex, SOQL, triggers, testing and Lightning Web Components fundamentals.

questions.prompt: How many SOQL queries can a **synchronous** Apex transaction issue before it fails?
questions.explanation: The synchronous limit is 100 SOQL queries per transaction (asynchronous Apex gets 200). Hitting it throws an uncatchable `System.LimitException`, which is why queries belong outside loops.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum number of **DML statements** in one Apex transaction?
questions.explanation: 150 DML statements per transaction. 10,000 is the limit on the number of *records* processed by DML, a different limit.

questions.prompt: In a `before insert` trigger, which statement is true?

options.text: `Trigger.old` contains the records as they were before the insert
`Trigger.newMap` is null because the records do not have Ids yet
Field changes to `Trigger.new` require an `update` DML statement to save

questions.explanation: Records have no Ids before insert, so there is no `newMap`; `Trigger.old` only exists for update and delete. In *before* triggers you change `Trigger.new` directly — no DML needed.

questions.prompt: When a record is saved, which of these runs **first**?

options.text: A before-save (fast field update) record-triggered flow

questions.explanation: Before-save record-triggered flows run before Apex before triggers. Custom validation rules run after before triggers, and after triggers run once the record is saved to the database (not yet committed).

questions.prompt: A single DML statement inserts **1,000** Account records. How many times does an Account trigger execute?
questions.explanation: Triggers process records in chunks of 200, so 1,000 records invoke the trigger 5 times. Governor limits are shared across those chunks within the transaction — another reason to bulkify.

questions.prompt: Which exception **cannot** be caught with a `try/catch` block?
questions.explanation: Exceeding a governor limit throws `System.LimitException`, which always terminates the transaction. Prevent it (check `Limits` methods, bulkify) rather than catching it.

questions.prompt: What does `Database.insert(records, false)` do differently from `insert records`?

options.text: It runs without enforcing validation rules
It allows partial success: valid records are saved and failures are reported in the results

questions.explanation: The second argument is `allOrNone`. With `false`, records that pass are committed and each failure is returned in a `Database.SaveResult` instead of throwing a `DmlException`.

questions.prompt: A class declared **without** any sharing keyword is called from a `with sharing` class. Which sharing rules apply to its code?

options.text: The sharing mode of the calling class (`with sharing` here)

questions.explanation: A class with no sharing declaration runs in the sharing mode of whatever called it. Declaring `inherited sharing` makes that explicit — the recommended practice for utility classes.

questions.prompt: Which **two** techniques protect dynamic SOQL built from user input against SOQL injection? *(Choose 2)*

options.text: Using bind variables such as `:name` in `Database.query`

questions.explanation: Bind variables keep input as data; `String.escapeSingleQuotes` neutralises quotes when concatenation is unavoidable. Exception handling and sharing modes do nothing against injection.

questions.prompt: Which decorator makes a Lightning Web Component property settable by its **parent** component?
questions.explanation: `@api` marks a public property or method. `@wire` binds data from an adapter or Apex; `@track` is only needed for deep reactivity of objects and arrays.

questions.prompt: An Apex method will be called from an LWC with `@wire`. What must its annotation include?
questions.explanation: Wired Apex methods must be `@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)`, which also means they cannot perform DML. Methods that change data are called imperatively instead.

questions.prompt: In a test class with the default `SeeAllData=false`, which existing org records can the test query?
questions.explanation: Tests are isolated from org data by default, but some setup data stays visible — including User and Profile records. Business data such as Accounts must be created by the test.

questions.prompt: What happens when `Test.stopTest()` is called?

options.text: Governor limits are reset to their original values
Asynchronous work enqueued since `Test.startTest()` runs synchronously before execution continues
All test data is rolled back

questions.explanation: `Test.startTest()` gives the code under test a fresh set of limits; `Test.stopTest()` forces queued async work (future, Queueable, Batch) to finish so you can assert on its results.

questions.prompt: Which coverage rules must be met to deploy Apex to production? *(Choose 2)*

options.text: At least 75% of all Apex code is covered by tests
Every trigger has some test coverage
Every test method contains at least one assertion

questions.explanation: Production deploys need 75% overall coverage and some coverage for every trigger. Assertions are best practice — coverage without assertions proves very little — but the platform doesn't enforce them.

questions.prompt: A child object must be deleted automatically when its parent record is deleted. Which relationship provides this?
questions.explanation: Deleting a master record deletes its detail records. A lookup can be configured to clear the field or block the delete, but a master-detail relationship always cascades.

questions.prompt: Where can a declarative **roll-up summary** field be created?

options.text: On the child of a lookup relationship
On the master object of a master-detail relationship
On any object with a formula field

questions.explanation: Roll-up summary fields live on the master side of a master-detail relationship (plus a few standard pairs such as Account → Opportunity). Lookups need Apex, flows or third-party tools to roll up.

questions.prompt: Which Apex collection automatically ignores duplicate values?
questions.explanation: A `Set` holds unique elements, which is why it's the usual way to gather record Ids before a bulk query. Lists (and array syntax, which is a List) keep duplicates; Map keys are unique but values aren't.

questions.prompt: In an LWC template, what must each element rendered inside `for:each` have?
questions.explanation: The engine uses `key` to track list items between renders, and the template won't compile without one. Use a stable value such as a record Id, not the loop index.

questions.prompt: A child Lightning Web Component needs to tell its parent that a value changed. What's the standard approach?

options.text: Set a property on the parent directly
Dispatch a `CustomEvent` that the parent handles
Write to a shared global variable

questions.explanation: Data flows down through `@api` properties and up through events: the child dispatches a `CustomEvent` (often with a `detail` payload) and the parent listens with `on<eventname>`.

questions.prompt: Which annotation creates test records once, for every test method in the class to use?
questions.explanation: A `@TestSetup` method runs once before the class's test methods. Each test method gets the records it created (rolled back between methods), which saves both time and code.

questions.prompt: In a **before insert** trigger, which context variable is null?
questions.explanation: Insert has no previous version, so Trigger.old and Trigger.oldMap are null. Trigger.newMap is also null in before insert, because records don't have Ids yet.

questions.prompt: Which query returns Accounts with their Contacts?

options.text: SELECT Name, (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts) FROM Account
SELECT Name, (SELECT LastName FROM Contact) FROM Account
SELECT Name FROM Account JOIN Contact

questions.explanation: Parent-to-child subqueries use the child relationship name, which is plural for standard objects (Contacts) and ends in __r for custom ones.

questions.prompt: Which is a valid custom exception class declaration?
questions.explanation: Custom exceptions extend Exception and their name must end with "Exception".

questions.prompt: How long does the value of a **static** Apex variable last?
questions.explanation: Static variables are reset for each transaction. That's why they work as recursion guards inside one save, but can't cache data between requests.

questions.prompt: What is the synchronous Apex heap size limit?
questions.explanation: 6 MB synchronous, 12 MB asynchronous.

questions.prompt: In LWC, when is `@track` still needed?

options.text: For every field shown in the template
To re-render when a property inside an object or an element of an array changes

questions.explanation: All fields are reactive when reassigned. `@track` is only needed to observe changes inside an object or array without reassigning it.

questions.prompt: Which SOQL clause enforces object permissions, field-level security and sharing for the running user?
questions.explanation: WITH USER_MODE runs the query as the user, enforcing CRUD, FLS and sharing. WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED checks only CRUD and FLS on the queried fields.

questions.prompt: Which is true about classes annotated `@isTest`?

options.text: They count toward the org's Apex code size limit
They don't count toward the org's Apex code size limit
They can be called from production code
They run with SeeAllData=true by default

questions.explanation: Test classes don't count toward the 6 MB Apex code limit. They can't be called from non-test code, and since API 24.0 they don't see org data by default.
